items.title: Section: Vajra-Like Concentration — The Final Blow That Severs Every Remaining Seed

items.zh: 彼即於此攝樂作意親近、修習、多修習故，有能無餘永斷修道所斷煩惱最後學位喻如金剛三摩地生。由此生故，便能永斷修道所斷一切煩惱。
items.en: Through closely cultivating and thoroughly cultivating this very gathering-joy engagement, at the final stage of one still in training, a concentration likened to a diamond arises, able to permanently and entirely sever whatever the path of cultivation is meant to sever. Because this arises, one is thereby able to permanently sever every affliction the path of cultivation severs.

items.zh: 問：何因緣故，此三摩地名金剛喻？答：
譬如金剛，望餘一切末尼、真珠、琉璃、螺貝、璧玉、珊瑚等諸珍寶，最為堅固；能穿、能壞所餘寶物，非餘寶物所能穿壞。如是此三摩地，於諸有學三摩地中，最上、最勝、最為堅固；能壞一切所有煩惱，非上煩惱所能蔽伏。是故此三摩地名金剛喻。
items.en: Just as a diamond, compared with every other precious substance — gemstone, pearl, lapis lazuli, conch shell, jade, coral, and the rest — is the most unbreakable, able to cut and pierce every other precious substance while none of them can cut or pierce it in turn … so too this concentration, among every concentration still belonging to one in training, is the highest, the most excellent, the most unbreakable; able to destroy every affliction whatsoever, with no affliction of the higher realms able to obscure or suppress it in return. For this reason, this concentration is called diamond-like.

items.title: Section: MAJOR — Arhatship Itself: Every Seed Gone, Freely Abiding, the Banner of Pride Cast Down

items.zh: 從此金剛喻三摩地，無間永害一切煩惱品麁重種子，其心於彼究竟解脫，證得畢竟種姓清淨。於諸煩惱究竟盡中，發起盡智。由因盡故，當來苦果畢竟不生，即於此中起無生智。彼於爾時，成阿羅漢，諸漏已盡，所作已辦，無復所作，證得自義，盡諸有結。已正奉行如來聖教，心善解脫。
items.en: Immediately following this diamond-like concentration, without any gap, every coarse seed of every kind of affliction is permanently destroyed, and the mind attains ultimate liberation with respect to them, realising the utterly pure nature that was always its final destiny … at that time, one becomes an arhat: the contaminants are exhausted, what was to be done is done, there is nothing further to do, one's own true benefit is realised, every fetter binding one to existence is exhausted. One has rightly carried out the Tathāgata's teaching in full, and the mind is thoroughly liberated.

items.zh: 已具成就十無學法。謂無學正見、正思惟，乃至無學正解脫、正智。於諸住中及作意中，能隨己心自在而轉。隨所樂住或聖、或天、或梵住中，即能安住。隨樂思惟所有正法，能引世間或出世間諸善義利，即能思惟。言聖住者，謂空住、無願住、無相住、滅盡定住。言天住者，謂諸靜慮，諸無色住。言梵住者，謂慈住、悲住、喜住、捨住。又於爾時，至極究竟，畢竟無垢，畢竟證得梵行邊際。
離諸關鍵，已出深坑，已度深塹。已能摧伏彼伊師迦，是為真聖，摧滅高幢。
items.en: Free of every bolt and lock, one has climbed out of the deep pit, crossed the deep moat, and subdued that towering Iṣīkā mountain — this is the true noble one, who has cast down pride's own high banner.

items.title: A Real Monastic, Defined: Five Things Abandoned, Five Attained, Four Requisites Guarded

items.zh: 已斷五支，成就六支。一向守護四所依止。
items.en: Having abandoned five factors, one has accomplished six factors … one guards, without exception, the four things one depends upon.

items.title: Section: The Monk Bitten by a Snake — Equanimity Tested at the Moment of Death

items.zh: 最極遠離，獨一諦實，棄捨希求，無濁思惟，身行猗息。
items.en: Utterly and finally free, singular and true, having relinquished all seeking, thought unclouded, bodily conduct wholly at ease.

items.zh: 心善解脫，慧善解脫。獨一無侶，正行已立，名已親近無上丈夫。具足成就六恒住法。謂眼見色已，無喜無憂，安住上捨，正念正知。如是耳聞聲已、鼻嗅香已、舌甞味已、身覺觸已、意了法已，無喜無憂，安住上捨，正念正知。彼於爾時，領受貪欲無餘永盡，領受瞋恚無餘永盡，領受愚癡無餘永盡。彼貪瞋癡皆永盡故，不造諸惡，習近諸善。其心猶如虛空淨水，如妙香檀，普為一切天帝天王恭敬供養。住有餘依般涅槃界，度生死海，已到彼岸。亦名任持最後有身。先業煩惱所引諸蘊自然滅故，餘取無故，不相續故，於無餘依般涅槃界而般涅槃。此中都無般涅槃者，如於生死無流轉者。唯有眾苦永滅、寂靜、清涼、滅沒。唯有此處最為寂靜。所謂棄捨一切所依，愛盡、離欲、永滅、涅槃。當知此中，有如是相。阿羅漢苾芻諸漏永盡，不能習近五種處所。一者、不能故思殺害諸眾生命；二者、不能不與而取；三者、不能行非
梵行習婬欲法；四者、不能知而妄語；五者、不能貯畜受用諸欲資具。如是不能妄計苦樂自作、他作、自他俱作、非自他作無因而生。又亦不能怖畏一切不應記事；又亦不能於雲、雷電、霹靂、災雹，及見種種怖畏事已，深生驚怖。當知此中，金剛喻定所攝作意，名加行究竟作意。最上阿羅漢果所攝作意，名加行究竟果作意。由如是等多種作意，依出世道
items.en: The holy life stands wonderfully accomplished, the noble path has been well cultivated; when life's span ends, one feels only joy — like setting down a jar of poison.

blocks.text: The end of the path: the diamond-like concentration and arhatship. Two passages (0477a15, 0477a28) are untranslated.

At the final stage of training, "a concentration likened to a diamond arises, able to sever whatever the path of cultivation is meant to sever". "Just as a diamond, compared with every other gem (pearl, lapis, conch, jade, coral), is the most unbreakable, able to cut every other while none can cut it", so this concentration "destroys every affliction, with none above it able to obscure it".

"Immediately following it, every coarse seed of affliction is permanently destroyed, and the mind attains ultimate liberation, realising the utterly pure nature that was always its final destination." "Free of every bolt and lock, one has climbed out of the deep pit, crossed the moat, subdued the towering Iṣīkā mountain: the true noble one, who has cast down pride's high banner."

"Mind well liberated, wisdom well liberated; alone, without companion." The arhat has the **six constant abidings**: seeing a form, hearing a sound, and so on, "without joy, without sorrow, abiding in supreme equanimity, mindful and clearly knowing". Greed, hatred, and delusion are exhausted. "The mind is like space, like pure water, like fine sandalwood." Living, such a one abides in nirvāṇa with remainder; at death, the aggregates cease of themselves, and there is nirvāṇa without remainder: "and here no one attains nirvāṇa, just as no one wanders in saṃsāra" (Day 131). The arhat cannot deliberately kill, steal, or engage in sexual conduct, and so on.

subs.head: Like setting down a jar of poison

blocks.text: "The holy life stands accomplished, the noble path well cultivated; when life's span ends, one feels only joy, like setting down a jar of poison."

quiz.q: Why is this concentration "called diamond-like," according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: diamond is hardest — it pierces other gems, none pierce it
quiz.why: "Able to cut and pierce every other precious substance while none of them can cut or pierce it in turn." Master Cháng Bǎi: diamond is the hardest; it can pierce other gems, and no other gem can pierce it.

quiz.q: "Not obscured by 上煩惱" — rendered "no affliction above it." How do the masters read 上煩惱?
options: both: upper-realm afflictions of form and formless, the subtlest
quiz.why: "Able to destroy every affliction whatsoever, with no affliction above it able to obscure or suppress it in return." Venerable Miào Jìng: 上煩惱 are the afflictions of the form and formless realms, the subtlest. Master Cháng Bǎi: no upper-stage affliction can obscure or suppress it. The English is ambiguous.

quiz.q: The arhat "has subdued that Iṣīkā." What is Iṣīkā, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: a tall mountain outside Rājagṛha, an image for pride's height and firmness
quiz.why: "Subdued that towering Iṣīkā mountain — this is the true noble one, who has cast down pride's own high banner." Venerable Miào Jìng: outside Rājagṛha is a great high mountain named Iṣīkā; it's an image for pride, as tall and firm as Iṣīkā.

quiz.q: The arhat's "bodily conduct 猗息." How do the masters read 猗?
options: Miào Jìng: a particle without meaning; Cháng Bǎi: a particle, or else "ease"
quiz.why: "Utterly and finally free, singular and true, having relinquished all seeking, thought unclouded, bodily conduct wholly at ease." Venerable Miào Jìng: 猗 here is a verbal particle with no meaning of its own. Master Cháng Bǎi: 猗 is a particle, or it means ease. The English "wholly at ease" follows the latter.

quiz.q: "Abandoned five factors, accomplished six" — rendered "accomplished the remaining factors." What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: 《披尋記》 suspects 六 should be 五; Cháng Bǎi: the six are the six constant abidings. The English sidesteps "six."
quiz.why: "Having abandoned five factors, one has accomplished the remaining factors." Venerable Miào Jìng: the author of 《披尋記》 suspects the 六 in "six factors" should be 五. Master Cháng Bǎi: accomplishing six factors, as the text below says, means accomplishing the six constant abidings. The English avoids the number.
